<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **93** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**34** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b02484e13a2e43f12d2c942e9a8966ece9cfa31e`.

⛔ **16** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `master_detail (literal, 46 pages)`
- **13** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **175** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b02484e13a2e43f12d2c942e9a8966ece9cfa31e` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `6e68c86c41f74211100d3ebc7dbbde8f9d1317ae` — the merge of head `7c71a0de528557df74e7838783169e6edd9a14e6` into base `b02484e13a2e43f12d2c942e9a8966ece9cfa31e`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 6e68c86c41f74211100d3ebc7dbbde8f9d1317ae && git checkout 6e68c86c41f74211100d3ebc7dbbde8f9d1317ae
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin b02484e13a2e43f12d2c942e9a8966ece9cfa31e 7c71a0de528557df74e7838783169e6edd9a14e6 && git checkout -B drift-repro b02484e13a2e43f12d2c942e9a8966ece9cfa31e && git merge --no-ff 7c71a0de528557df74e7838783169e6edd9a14e6

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b02484e13a2e43f12d2c942e9a8966ece9cfa31e
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs b02484e13a2e43f12d2c942e9a8966ece9cfa31e` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## L1 review · REWORK · 2026-11-18T19:29Z

Head: `e45bb8924006679f9584e30470fe306ed893e450` (merge base `f2078e3674`). Read: the whole net diff (38 files), the PR body, claims 6983865455 (#34776) and 6983892347 (#35146), amendment 6987471285, seat note 6988981894 and dev report 6988884686.

### Checklist

- **Closing keywords**: `Fixes #34776` and `Fixes #35146`. Both cards are completed here. #35146's draft-door clause is the deviation the amendment accepted: the probes read what landed, whichever door wrote it, and that is where the card's symptom shows. I accept `Fixes` for it.
- **File surface**: every path is inside the two claims and the amendment. That covers the examples (Q1 A) and the ADR-0087 entry `18.publish-refuses-metadata-the-runtime-ignores.ts` (Q2 A).
- **Host refactor**: `draftVerdictHost()` carries every member the removed inline host of `assertRuntimeAuthoringRules` had, plus `sealedFlowNodeTypeVocabulary`. The two can no longer drift, as the comment says.
- **Changeset, sentence by sentence**:
  - Four packages at `minor`, with `Clause-②: no (narrowing …)`, `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` and the ADR-0087 `registered` marker. Right for six new publish refusals.
  - The six rule bullets match the validators and their severities. That includes `flow-http-timeout-missing` as a warning, and `flow-node-type-no-executor` judged only against `getSealedNodeTypeVocabulary()`, which answers `undefined` before sealing.
  - The four probes are warnings, and the `RuntimeBuildIssueSchema` describes list them. `RunBuildProbesOptions` gains `automation` and `packageId`.
  - The new exports named are the ones the barrels add.
  - The `Skills-docs:` line still reads `follow-up owed`. See R3.
- **Examples**: each `initialStates` matches the field's default and the comment beside it. The opportunity list (every stage) is argued from `OpportunityStageHook`'s insert path. The three update-only machines are declarative only; the seat chose B, and #35251 is filed and open. The four `timeoutMs: 10000` additions satisfy the new warning.
- **Narrowing battery**: dev report 6988884686 pins `@objectstack/dogfood` to `e45bb89240`: 481 files and 4082 tests passed, and the closure build is clean.
- **CI on this head**: red. `Test Core (7/10)` failed, and 24 runs are still in progress. See R1.
- **Main since the merge base**: no commit on `main` touches the hand-written files of this diff.
- **Governed check**: `check-governed-merges --pr 35244`: not governed (0 of 38 paths), 1,896 changed lines.

### REWORK

- **R1 (CI red)**: `packages/core/src/security/second-object-read-exposure.pin.test.ts` (#22661) fails on this head: `packages/metadata-protocol/src/build-probes.ts` now calls `referenceTargetOf` (the seed-reference probe, and `childForeignKey` for the roll-up probe), and the pin's `CALLERS` does not classify it. Classify it in `CALLERS` under the class that is true of it, with the reason the pin asks for. The dogfood battery does not run `packages/core`'s `test:repo` leg, so it could not see this.
- **R2**: in the same probes, the sample reads are organisation-scoped (`scoped(organizationId)`), but the `id $in` read of the reference target (`seed_reference_unresolved`) and the parent read (`rollup_never_computed`) are not. The seed probe claims to find exactly the values the edit form refuses (`reference_not_found`), and the form judges inside the organisation. Scope both reads as the sample read is scoped, or state in the code, and in the R1 classification, why the unscoped read is the right judge. Add one case for it to `build-probes-landed-data.test.ts`.
- **R3**: the changeset's `Skills-docs:` line still reads `follow-up owed — skills/** traps for the six rules`. The card is filed: make it `follow-up #35245`, as the PR body already says.

These move the head. I will read only the delta, and CI on the new head.

### Notes (non-blocking)

- N1: the contract review (claim 6989008919) is its own record. Its findings, if any, can ride the same fix round.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `e45bb8924006679f9584e30470fe306ed893e450`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.publish-refuses-metadata-the-runtime-ignores.ts + packages/lint/src/authoring-rules.ts, packages/lint/src/lint-flow-patterns.ts, packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts, packages/lint/src/runtime-gate.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-action-object-binding.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-flow-node-executors.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-inert-object-declarations.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/build-probes.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/build-probes.user-text.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-authoring-gate.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-history-and-publish.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/runtime-authoring-gate.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/engine.ts, examples/app-crm/src/objects/lead.object.ts, examples/app-crm/src/objects/opportunity.object.ts, examples/app-showcase/src/data/objects/account.object.ts, examples/app-showcase/src/data/objects/project.object.ts, examples/app-showcase/src/data/objects/task.object.ts, examples/app-showcase/src/automation/flows/index.ts, examples/app-showcase/src/automation/flows/exchange-rate-sync.flow.ts

First full review of PR #35244 (cards #34776 and #35146). Read: both cards with every comment, ruling 6940528935, claims 6983865455 and 6983892347, amendment 6987471285, seat note 6988981894, the PR body, the net diff against `main`, and the head's check-runs. Code outside the diff was read at the head to judge the diff: `ui/packages/core`, `ui/packages/components`, `ui/apps/console`, `packages/objectql`, `packages/runtime`, `packages/services/service-automation`, `packages/platform-objects`, and the cloud sources the PR cites.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Six publish-time refusals (accept set narrowed at the runtime gate and the CLI).**
  - `flow-node-type-no-executor`: right. It is judged only against the set the engine's own audit uses (`knownNodeTypes()`: structural types, executors, action descriptors), read live, and only after the seal. `getSealedNodeTypeVocabulary()` answers `undefined` until `nodeTypeVocabularySealed` is set. No CLI path sets `flowNodeTypeVocabulary`, so the CLI judges nothing. The walk covers region bodies, as `unknownNodeTypes` does.
  - `flow-approval-decision-unrouted`: right. `APPROVAL_BRANCH_LABELS.approve` / `.reject` are the labels the approval service resumes with, and `traverseNext` falls back to every out-edge when no edge carries the label. A `revise` edge and a `fault` edge do not satisfy or trip the rule. An `isDefault` edge does not claim `approve` or `reject` in the engine, so requiring both labels is correct.
  - `flow-http-timeout-missing`: warning only, confirmed (`severity: 'warning'`, so it lands in `advisories`). Two logic gaps: S4.
  - `field-boolean-required`: wrong. See M1.
  - `state-machine-no-initial-states`: right as the card rules it, with the gaps in S3.
  - `action-no-object-binding`: verdict right. Every `ACTION_LOCATIONS` value is an object surface, and no renderer under `ui/` draws an object-less action by location. One reason sentence is false: N1.
- **Published spec (`protocol.zod.ts`).** Describes only; no type, key or accept set moves. The code list (12 codes), the `flow` artefact, the `connector` ref and the `member` sentence each match `build-probes.ts` at the head. The warning sentence does not: S6.
- **Published spec, not edited.** Two describes now disagree with the gate: `FieldSchema.required` (M1) and `initialStates` ("Omit to keep the legacy behavior", S3).
- **Public surface, additive, right.** `@objectstack/lint` exports three validators, their finding types and six rule ids; `AuthoringRuleContext.flowNodeTypeVocabulary`; `runRuntimeAuthoringRules` and `evaluateRuntimeAuthoringGate` gain an optional argument; `RunBuildProbesOptions.automation` / `.packageId` and `ProbeAutomation`; `AutomationEngine.getSealedNodeTypeVocabulary()`; four members on `RuntimeBuildIssueCode`.
- **Probe severities.** All four new probes emit `warning`. Nothing in them fails a publish: they run after the promotion, and a throw is swallowed (`probes = undefined`).
- **Docs transcripts 70 to 73.** Right: three registry entries were added (two of the six rules live inside `lintFlowPatterns`, one entry holds two).
- **`protocol.ts` host.** Right. `draftVerdictHost()` spells the seven members `assertRuntimeAuthoringRules` reads exactly as the removed literal did (the same two getters, the same delegations). The eight extra members are outside `RuntimeRulesHost`. The only new read is `sealedFlowNodeTypeVocabulary`, on a flow write.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset: `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, `@objectstack/spec`, all `minor`. The kind is `narrowed`, which takes at least `minor` on each package the diff moves. Right.
- `Clause-②: no (narrowing: …)` and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` are on the PR body and the changeset, same wording. Right for refusals of metadata the schema accepts.
- `adr-0087: registered publish-refuses-metadata-the-runtime-ignores` names the id of the entry in the diff. `Check Changeset` and `Lint · CI, release & engine gates` are green on the head.
- The registry, `spec-changes` and the upgrade guide are generated from the entry file (`registry.ts.template`); none is committed, so the diff carries no generated output to disagree with it.
- Changeset prose that does not match the tree: the `field-boolean-required` line (M1), "routes no decision" (S5), "so the edit form cannot save it" (S2), and `Skills-docs: follow-up owed` where the PR body says `follow-up #35245` (N3).

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Q1 (examples), seat answer A.** Done as answered. `crm_opportunity` listing all five stages is honest: `opportunity.hook.ts` runs on `beforeInsert`, and `test/opportunity-stage-hook.test.ts` inserts `closed_won`, `closed_lost` and `proposal`. The five stages are every option the `stage` field has, so the list refuses nothing. See S3. `timeoutMs: 10000` is sane: it is the value the rule's own hint names, and the engine has no default.
- **Q2 (ledger), seat answer A.** Done. Content findings: M1, S5.
- **Q3 (update-only machines), seat answer B, follow-up #35251.** Accepted as recorded. Two more inert cases are not carried by #35251: S3.
- **Draft-door deviation (#35146).** The stated reason holds for three probes. It does not hold for `flow_connector_action_unresolved`: that probe reads the flow body and the engine's connector lookups and no landed record, so the draft door could carry it. Escalated to the seat: amend the deviation line or file a follow-up card.
- **Surface breaches the dev declared.** Each is covered by amendment 6987471285.
- **Dev account against the tree.** The reports say 131 families derived and run with every family at exit 0. The head's `Test Core (7/10)` is red on a `packages/core` `test:repo` pin that names this diff: M2.
- **SQL push-down.** The roll-up and seed probes materialise ids in application code (a child sample, then `id $in` on the parent or target) and read whole rows. The reads are bounded at 50 rows, with one or two reads per roll-up field and per reference column, and no per-record loop. No reason is given for not projecting or pushing the join down: S1.
- **Not measured from this seat.** Whether a declarative connector published in the same batch is registered before the connector probe runs. If the reconcile is later, the probe warns once on a step that will work.
- **Out of scope, carried.** Skills traps: #35245. M1 changes what that card should teach about a required checkbox.

### ④ Design judgment

**M1 (must-fix) — `field-boolean-required` refuses metadata that works at the head, on a reason the tree contradicts.**
- The rule's reason, in its finding, its explanation, the changeset and the ledger entry: `required` on a `boolean` / `toggle` "guards nothing", and "the record form reads it as must be checked and refuses to save the box unchecked".
- The form: `ui/packages/core/src/validation/required-presence.ts` states that `false` is not absent, names cloud#972 as the defect it closed, and is the predicate the form renderer's `required` validator calls (`ui/packages/components/src/renderers/form/form.tsx`, `!isMissingForRequired(value)`), as does the console `FormPage` and the wizard. The same renderer seeds an untouched two-state control with `false` on create. An unchecked required box saves, with or without a `defaultValue`.
- The server: `FieldSchema.required` is published as "an insert must provide a non-null value, and an update may not null it out", and `record-validator.ts` enforces that on a boolean (`isEmptyForRequired`: `null` and absent are empty, `false` is not). So the flag does guard something: a `null` written by an API caller or a PATCH.
- The remedy the rule prescribes (remove `required`, add `defaultValue: false`) makes `null` storable on update. That is a declared capability taken away, not a dead declaration removed.
- The platform's own objects carry the shape: `sys_webhook.active`, `sys_job.active`, `sys_email_template.active`, `sys_scim_connection_credential.active` (each `required: true, defaultValue: true`) and `sys_scim_user.active` (`required: true`, no default).
- The cited source (`graph-lint.ts`, cloud) grades the same condition a warning.
- The card's premise for this item ("the create form then refuses an unchecked switch") is no longer true of the tree. That is the seat's to take to the maintainer; the rule cannot ship as an error on it. The ledger entry and the changeset line move with whatever is decided.

**M2 (must-fix) — the head's `Test Core (7/10)` check-run is `failure`.**
- `packages/core` `test:repo`, `src/security/second-object-read-exposure.pin.test.ts`, "every caller of the reference-target arbiter is classified": `packages/metadata-protocol/src/build-probes.ts` now calls `referenceTargetOf` and is not in `CALLERS`.
- The pin asks for a classification, and for a read that serves anything of the target to ask the target's exposure first. The answer belongs with S1, which is about the same reads.

**S1 (should-fix) — the roll-up and seed probes read under a bare `{ isSystem: true }` context, read whole rows, and quote row values back.**
- The parent read and the target read are not scoped the way the sample reads and the engine's own referential-integrity audit are; scope them the same way.
- `engine-referential-integrity.ts` records why the engine stopped doing this (#19808: a bare system probe "spanned every organization"; #19837: the audit passes the scanned row's own organization). `ObjectQL.inspectDanglingReferences` already does this scan with that posture.
- Effects: the judgement can disagree with what the engine answers the caller (`reference_not_found`), and `seed_reference_unresolved.message` quotes up to five values; project only the fields the probe needs and quote only values read in scope.
- The sample is any 50 rows of the object, not the seed's rows, so a dangle in user data is reported as the seed's.
- No `fields` projection on any of the four reads, where the foreign key, the aggregated field, the roll-up field and `id` are all that is read.

**S2 (should-fix) — `seed_reference_unresolved` states a consequence the engine removed.**
- `message`: "the engine re-checks every reference in it, so those records cannot be saved, whichever field the user changed". `userMessage`, eleven locales: "cannot be saved after an edit".
- `assertReferencesResolve` forgives a value the row already stores (#29062: "the check judges only the references a write ADDS … an edit form carries the whole record back"). A stored dangling value does not block an edit.
- The finding itself (the column names no row) stands. The sentence about what the person will see does not.

**S3 (should-fix) — `state-machine-no-initial-states` accepts a declaration the runtime ignores, and the spec still documents the omission.**
- `initialStates: []` passes the rule (`!== undefined`). `checkStateMachine` treats an empty list as no contract ("legacy no-op"). The rule's stated purpose is not met, by the shortest edit that silences it.
- `validation.zod.ts` still describes the key with "Omit to keep the legacy behavior (no initial-state check on insert)". After this PR an omission is refused at publish.
- A list naming every option of the field (`crm_opportunity`, as its hook and tests require) refuses nothing either. Together with update-only machines this is a second and third inert case; #35251 names only the first.
- A machine with `active: false` is also reported, and never runs.

**S4 (should-fix) — `flow-http-timeout-missing` reads one of the two timeouts and accepts a value that arms none.**
- The engine races every node against node-level `timeoutMs` (`flow.zod.ts:776`, the line the card cites; `dag-traversal.ts`, `node.timeoutMs` greater than 0). An `http` node carrying it is warned that an endpoint "holds the run", which is untrue.
- `config.timeoutMs: 0` satisfies the rule, and the executor arms no timer for it (`timeoutMs ? setTimeout(…) : undefined`).
- A `durable: true` node with an outbox does not hold the run either; it is warned the same way.

**S5 (should-fix) — the ledger entry misstates the approval failure.**
- Entry `reason`: "an approval decision with no matching edge routes nowhere". Changeset: "routes no decision".
- `traverseNext`: the branch selection is ignored and every out-edge is evaluated. The rule's own finding and explanation say so correctly. The upgrade guide would tell an author the flow stops, when it runs both branches.

**S6 (should-fix) — the `severity` describe is untrue of two of the four codes it lists.**
- It places all four under "what landed reads in a way the person will notice although it may be the truth".
- `flow_connector_action_unresolved` reports a step that fails on every run that reaches it (its own `message`), and `seed_reference_unresolved` reports a value that names no row. Neither may be the truth. The `error` sentence beside it ("the published artifact is broken at runtime") describes the connector case better than the sentence it was filed under.
- "Neither fails the publish" is true.

**S7 (should-fix) — `rollup_never_computed` prescribes a repair that fixes one parent.**
- `fix` and `userMessage`: write or edit one child row to recalculate. A child write recomputes the parents that child names, not the N parents the finding counts.
- `message`: "a roll-up recalculates only when a child row is written". `summary-aggregate.ts` lists three writers, and the platform's repair for exactly this state is `os migrate summary-nulls --apply`; an install door also materialises new roll-ups (`summary-install-materialise.ts`).
- The judgement itself is sound: only parents a sampled child points at, only a field unset on all of them, a child with no value in the aggregated field is not counted, a filtered roll-up is skipped, and the foreign key is resolved as the engine resolves it.

Nits:
- **N1 (nit)** — `action-no-object-binding` says a call on an object's action route answers "not found" (finding, explanation, two comments). An object-less declaration owns every route (`standaloneActionOwnsRoute`, `actionHandlerObjectKeys`), so the call resolves. The verdict does not depend on the sentence.
- **N2 (nit)** — `widget_empty_result`: the comment says an empty answer to a caller who sees no rows is not reported. That holds for a result with no rows; a no-dimension aggregate answering `0` over an object with no rows is one row and is reported. The `fix` names the widget's time window and condition, which the probe's selection does not send. It does not duplicate `empty_query`: the two are one `if / else if`, and `everyMeasureZero` is false on an empty result.
- **N3 (nit)** — the changeset's `Skills-docs:` line reads `follow-up owed`; the PR body reads `follow-up #35245`.
- **N4 (nit)** — `ref` is described as present "when that is not the artifact itself"; the roll-up finding's `ref` is the artefact's own object with a `member`.

Held against the tree and found right: the connector probe asks `resolveConnectorInstanceFor`, `resolveConnectorAction` and `getConnectorDegradedReason` in the executor's order (`builtin/connector-nodes.ts`), with the publishing package, and a lookup that throws judges nothing. The runtime gate charges a finding on the written item itself and cancels a sibling's, so "the next publish or write is refused, nothing is rewritten, nothing is refused at boot" in the ledger entry is true; a draft save, the package-author channel and `migrate-stored` are not judged.

Check-runs on the head when this record was written: 72 runs; 46 success, 12 skipped, 1 failure (`Test Core (7/10)`, M2), 13 still in progress (`Test Core` 1, 9 and 10 of 10; `Type Check UI`; nine `Test UI` shards). Green and named in this record's judgments: `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards`, `Spec property liveness`, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`, `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Build Core`, `Build Docs`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-34776-publish-checks-build-probes`
Reviewed-by: `session_01JQwxbXGvw43spR79ztEvWt`

**VERDICT: FAIL**
